page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c5.2xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1494.09 and 7865.45 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 4531.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 437.77 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks, dropping to 50.41 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation with a score of 7261.0 and static web serving throughput of 7.26 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing, and poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing for a 7B model which registers at 11.09 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of bundled local storage or specialized GPU accelerators. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. Recommended workloads include batch processing, distributed analytics, web serving, and moderate scientific modeling or software compilation.
